title: Installing Packages
description: Learn how to install, update, and remove dependencies with NPM and Yarn.

data.text: Installing packages is the most frequent task in JavaScript development. NPM and Yarn offer similar commands with slightly different syntax.
Production dependencies are required for your app to run. Development dependencies are only needed during development, such as testing libraries or bundlers.

data.caption: Install Express as a production dependency
data.code:
npm install express
# or
yarn add express

data.caption: Install Jest as a development dependency
data.code:
npm install --save-dev jest
# or
yarn add --dev jest

data.title: Global Installs
data.text: Global packages (e.g., eslint, typescript) are installed with -g flag. Use sparingly; prefer local installs per project.
By default, caret (^) allows minor updates while tilde (~) allows only patch updates. Both managers respect these ranges in package.json.

terms.definition: Required for the app to run in production.
Available across all projects on the machine.

items.question: Why use local over global installs?
items.answer: Local installs ensure the exact version is used by every contributor and CI environment.

items.question: What happens if I install without saving?
items.answer: In older NPM versions, you had to use --save. Modern NPM and Yarn save by default.

items.text: Production vs dev dependencies serve different purposes.
